advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor workflow run-block line numbers to the step's actual YAML position instead of first-substring match, which collides on shared opening lines like `set -euo pipefail`.
evidence: 554: def _first_line_of(text_lines: list[str], needle: str) -> int:
557:         for i, line in enumerate(text_lines, start=1):
558:             if target in line:
559:                 return i
573:         base_line = _first_line_of(file_lines, run.splitlines()[0] if run.splitlines() else "")
reconcile-bridge.yml uses `set -euo pipefail` as the first run line (line 284), a pattern shared by multiple steps in the same file
advisory.finding: `_first_line_of` maps a workflow run-block to the FIRST file line containing the block's first text line; steps whose run block begins with a common line (e.g. `set -euo pipefail`) collide and all map to the same `base_line`, so reported violation line numbers point at the wrong step.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Report `marker-without-reason` at `base_line + (marker_line - 1)` using the collected empty-marker line index rather than a flat `base_line`.
evidence: 503:         reasons, empty_markers = _collect_markers(lines)
504:     violations = [
505:         Violation(
506:             rel, base_line, "marker-without-reason", "raw-git-ok marker requires a reason"
508:         for _ in empty_markers
`_collect_markers` returns the 1-based line index within the block, but it is discarded (`for _ in empty_markers`) in favor of `base_line`
advisory.finding: Empty `# raw-git-ok:` markers found inside a shell/workflow block are all reported at `base_line`, not at the marker's real line, so the `marker-without-reason` violation points at the wrong line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In `_check_wrapper_call`, resolve the subcommand position via `_git_subcommand` semantics rather than scanning every string arg for a mutation verb.
evidence: 360:         verb = next((t for t in tokens if t in MUTATION_VERBS), None)
338:     def _check_wrapper_call(self, call: ast.Call, name: str) -> None:
Contrast with the raw-subprocess path which calls `_git_subcommand(tokens)` (line 332) to isolate the subcommand position and skip option forms
advisory.finding: The wrapper-call check flags a mutation verb appearing in ANY string argument position, not the git subcommand position, so a legitimate non-mutating call whose literal argument equals a verb (e.g. a pathspec or commit message `add`) false-positives; conversely git global options are not skipped.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the line-above-def marker match so a marker attached to a prior statement cannot leak onto the following def.
evidence: 153:         first_line = min([func.lineno] + [d.lineno for d in func.decorator_list])
154:         candidates = [first_line - 1, func.lineno]

advisory.finding: `_function_marker` treats the line directly above the def (`first_line - 1`) as a sanction source; a `# raw-git-ok:` comment belonging to a preceding statement or an adjacent def can silently over-sanction the following function.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or guard) that local argv tracking is branch-order-sensitive because branches share and overwrite the same tracking dicts.
evidence: 233:             for tgt in stmt.targets:
234:                 if isinstance(tgt, ast.Name):
235:                     self.local_lists[tgt.id] = elements  # None => untracked
409:             for inner in self._nested_bodies(stmt):
410:                 self.run(inner)
module header documents intra-function tracking as best-effort residual but does not call out branch-order sensitivity
advisory.finding: Local argv tracking mutates shared linter state across control-flow branches: `run()` recurses into `if/for/try` bodies on the same `_ScopeLinter` instance, and `_track` unconditionally overwrites `local_lists`/`local_strs`, so a variable assigned differently in two branches resolves to whichever branch was visited last.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Layer-P test that a resolved argv list with a non-literal head element (e.g. sys.executable / a path variable) followed by a mutation verb does NOT fire.
evidence: Source: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:322-329 — `head = tokens[0]` / `if head is None:` / `# Resolved list with a non-literal head (sys.executable, a path variable): treated as non-git.`
Module header documents this as ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: 'a resolved argv list whose HEAD is a non-literal expression ... is treated as non-git'
ABSENCE: no test in test_raw_git_write_lint.py constructs an argv literal like `[sys.executable, ..., 'commit']` or `[some_path_var, 'add']` to assert it does NOT fire.
Module header: 'local scalar assignments like ``prog = "git"`` ARE tracked'
Source: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:230-236 — `local_strs` populated from string-Constant assigns; _resolve_elements at ~211 uses `self.local_strs.get(elt.id)`.
ABSENCE: no test assigns `prog = "git"` then builds argv `[prog, ..., 'commit']` to assert `raw-git-mutation` fires.
advisory.finding: The documented residual behavior 'a resolved argv list whose HEAD is a non-literal expression (sys.executable, a path variable) is treated as non-git' has no test. The source guard at scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:322-329 (`if head is None: return`) is a deliberate correctness boundary, but no fixture exercises a resolved list literal whose first element is a non-literal followed by a git mutation verb. A regression that made this branch fire (false positive) or that mishandled the head would not be caught.
merged_from: The 'local scalar prog = "git" IS tracked' capability — explicitly documented as distinguishing the lint from its accepted residual — has no test. local_strs tracking (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:_track / _resolve_elements) resolves a Name element via `self.local_strs.get(elt.id)`, but no fixture launders the git program name through a local scalar to confirm a mutation still fires.
scenarios: A future change reorders _git_subcommand/head handling so a resolved non-literal-head list starts firing (or crashes), producing false positives on non-git subprocess launches.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Layer-P test that a wrapper call with a single untracked plain-Name argv (e.g. `_run_git(argv)` with opaque `argv`) fires `unresolvable-argv-wrapper`.
evidence: Source: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:369-373 — `elif not tokens and untracked_names:` emits `unresolvable-argv-wrapper` `unresolvable argv to git wrapper` (distinct message from the starred branch).
Existing test only covers starred forwarding: test_wrapper_opaque_star_forwarding_fires_and_marker_silences uses `run_git(tracker, *args)`.
ABSENCE: no fixture calls a wrapper with a single untracked non-star Name argv, e.g. `_run_git(argv)` with `argv` an opaque param.
advisory.finding: The non-starred opaque-wrapper branch (`elif not tokens and untracked_names`) at scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:369-374 is untested. Only the STARRED opaque-forwarding case (`*args`) is covered (test_wrapper_opaque_star_forwarding_fires_and_marker_silences). A wrapper call receiving a single untracked plain Name argv (e.g. `_run_git(argv)` where `argv` is an unresolved parameter) exercises a different code path with the same `unresolvable-argv-wrapper` kind but distinct emission logic.
scenarios: A refactor of _check_wrapper_call breaks the non-star untracked-name accounting (untracked_names counting) while leaving the starred path intact — undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the Layer W sanction line-adjacent (or emit per-line hits) so each git mutation in a workflow run block requires its own `# raw-git-ok:` marker instead of one marker blanket-sanctioning the whole block.
evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:512 `sanction = next(iter(reasons.values()), None)  # any reasoned marker sanctions the block`
scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:523 `return [hit], violations  # one hit per block: the first offending line`

reconcile-bridge.yml:285 `# raw-git-ok: commit-back CAS push loop stays verbatim in YAML per ticket 4c4f` sanctions the block that then runs `git add -A` (291), `git commit` (292) and `git push` (316)
advisory.finding: The workflow-lint (Layer W) sanctions an entire multi-line run block with a single `# raw-git-ok:` marker and emits at most one hit per block, so the one marker added at reconcile-bridge.yml:285 blanket-sanctions `git add -A`, `git commit`, and `git push` — and any future git mutation inserted into that step rides the existing marker with no re-review, widening the blast radius of the very workflow write-path the gate is meant to guard.
scenarios: A future edit adds a new `git checkout`/`git reset`/`git rm` to the same commit-back step; the block-level marker suppresses the gate and the new mutation ships un-reviewed against origin/tickets.
